title: Silver Fir: Ancient Silver Firs You Can Visit
meta_description: Germany's tallest, thickest and oldest documented silver fir, a Danish cemetery giant and a Lithuanian roadside champion. Three mapped so far.
intro: A silver fir this old is rare precisely because the species is not: Abies alba covers mountain slopes across central Europe by the million, so a single named, dated, individually remarkable specimen stands out against a background of forestry. The Waldhaustanne in the Bayerischer Wald is the extreme case, Germany's tallest, thickest and oldest documented silver fir, unrecorded until a family out walking reported it in 2020: about 53 metres tall, 6.93 metres round and roughly 605 years old, home to 274 recorded species and reached by a boardwalk built to keep boots off its roots. Priekulė's, by contrast, earns its fame from restraint, a single fir a Lithuanian town thought worth its own signpost at a crossroads. Aarhus's stands forty and a half metres over a private family graveyard moved wholesale into Moesgård's park in 1926. Three mapped so far, each a fir that got singled out from a forest.
